answer.E: One chart reports the vacancy rate of Grade A office buildings in core business districts, while the other reports the vacancy rate of high-quality office buildings in core business districts. Different definitions may lead to inconsistent data.

answer.D: The net absorption volumes in Beijing and Shanghai are stable but lower than that in Shenzhen. This may be because the demand shares of the finance and professional services industries are high, which disperses the influence of the technology industry.
answer.E: Hangzhou has a net absorption volume of only 64,000 square meters and a vacancy rate of 16%. The technology demand has not effectively reduced the vacancy rate because the demand share of the manufacturing industry is higher.

qa_pairs.question: As a real estate investment company, based on the office building market data, how should the investment priorities in different cities be adjusted to minimize the vacancy risk and improve the return? Please select the most reasonable strategic suggestion.

answer.A: Give priority to investing in all first-tier cities (such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen) because these cities have developed economies and dense populations, which can naturally reduce the vacancy risk and improve the investment return.
answer.B: Give priority to investing in first-tier cities with low vacancy rates in core business districts and pay attention to cities with outstanding net absorption volume performance. Because these areas have stable demand and strong absorption capacity, they can effectively reduce the investment risk and increase the rental rate.
answer.C: Significantly reduce the rent level in cities with high vacancy rates (such as Shenyang and Dalian) to quickly attract tenants and reduce the vacant area, thereby improving the investment return.
answer.D: In cities where the vacancy rate in the core business district is much lower than that in the whole city (such as Beijing with 9.8% in the core vs 17.1% in the whole city), focus on investing in non-core areas because the large difference in vacancy rates means that non-core areas have higher potential and lower costs.
answer.E: Based on the fact that the technology industry has the highest leasing demand share (33.6%), give priority to developing office building projects in science and technology parks in all cities to utilize the high-demand industry to promote the rental rate.
answer.F: In second-tier cities with high vacancy rates, reduce investment in new development projects and instead attract tenants from high-demand industries (such as technology or finance) to revitalize the existing stock because these industries have the highest leasing demand share and can quickly improve the vacancy situation.
answer.G: In cities where there is a significant difference in the vacancy rate between the core business district and the whole city, focus on investing in the core area rather than the whole city scope because the vacancy rate in the core business district is generally lower and more resilient, which can ensure a more stable cash flow.

answer.E: Focus on targeted tenant recruitment for the technology and finance industries because these industries have the highest shares in leasing demand, which can significantly improve the leasing speed and reduce the vacancy rate in cities with high vacancy rates.
answer.F: In cities with high net absorption volume (such as Shenzhen with a net absorption volume of 641,000 square meters), ignore the vacancy rate data (19%) and directly expand the tenant recruitment scale to match the high absorption capacity and avoid future supply shortages.
answer.G: In cities where the vacancy rate in the core business district is low but the vacancy rate in the whole city is high, adopt a differentiated leasing strategy (such as maintaining high-end tenants in the core area and introducing cost-sensitive industries in non-core areas) to balance the overall market supply and demand.
